fact: TechHive Advisory reviews Angola's draft AI law, a risk-based framework governing development, supply and use of AI with human-centric safeguards.
source_slug: 2025-12-29 Review of Angola's Proposed Law on Artificial Intelligence

fact: CAZOS says the MINTTICS AI bill (86 articles, in public consultation since September 2025) would criminalise algorithmic discrimination and create an AI authority, and the APD's draft revision of Lei 22/11 has an AI chapter (arts. 36-38) banning algorithmic social scoring; neither is in force.
system: MINTTICS AI bill; APD revision of Lei 22/11

fact: CAZOS says Lei n.º 22/11 of 17 June, the data protection law in force, already governs decisions taken by automated means.
CAZOS says the Agência de Protecção de Dados (APD), created by Presidential Decree 214/16, supervises, has sanctioning powers, and is the first regulator to reach automated decisions in Angola.
Portal de TI reports that Angola's Proposta de Lei sobre a Inteligência Artificial is in public consultation, and that the country has no AI-specific legislation yet.
system: Proposta de Lei sobre a Inteligência Artificial

fact: APD legal director Njunjulo António says the right not to be subject to automated decisions already exists and that the agency's inspection and audit of AI use rests on data-processing principles of transparency, purpose and lawfulness.
system: Right not to be subject to automated decisions
